cohort: Pregnant women in Georgia, USA from 2008 to 2012
finding: Counties in Georgia, USA with high caesarean delivery rates had significantly lower access to midwives, more deliveries paid by Medicaid, a higher proportion of births for women belonging to racial/ethnic minority groups, and were more likely to be rural.
mod_finding: This study found that counties with higher cesarean delivery rates had lower access to midwives.
